title: IonQ Advances Quantum-Assured Navigation and Timing with DARPA Airborne Gravimeter Award and 51-Day Maritime Clock Trial - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IonQ's quantum sensing subsidiary Vector Atomic won a DARPA GRAVMAP Phase II Option for an airborne strapdown rubidium gravimeter (flight tests 2027) and completed a 51-day Navy-sponsored maritime deployment of its Evergreen-30 iodine optical clock, positioning IonQ in GPS-denied PNT for defense.

insights.claim: IonQ is targeting GPS-denied Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) for maritime and airborne defense platforms through its quantum sensing subsidiary Vector Atomic.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum sensing gives IonQ a nearer-term defense revenue line beyond quantum computing.
insights.locator: IonQ (NYSE: IONQ) has detailed two milestones

insights.claim: IonQ pairs passive gravitational and magnetic navigation sensors with optical atomic clocks to provide continuous timing resilience when satellite signals are jammed or spoofed.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: GPS jamming/spoofing is a growing defense concern; integrated quantum PNT stacks address it.
insights.locator: Complementing its passive gravitational and magnetic navigation sensors

insights.claim: Vector Atomic received a DARPA Phase II Option under the GRAVMAP program to develop an airborne strapdown rubidium atomic gravimeter, after completing top-level assembly vibration analysis.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Progressing to Phase II Option signals DARPA is satisfied with technical milestones — continued government funding for IonQ sensing.
insights.locator: PNT specifications table: DARPA GRAVMAP Gravimeter

insights.claim: The GRAVMAP gravimeter is designed to operate without active motion stabilization during representative flight dynamics by pairing a strapdown rubidium atomic sensor with conventional inertial sensors for vibration immunity.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Removing motion-stabilization gimbals cuts SWaP, making quantum gravimetry deployable on aircraft.
insights.locator: Under DARPA's Gravimeter using Rubidium Atoms

insights.claim: Vector Atomic will complete GRAVMAP system integration and laboratory characterization through the remainder of 2026, with airborne platform demonstrations in 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: 2027 flight tests are the next catalyst for IonQ's sensing business.
insights.locator: Under DARPA's Gravimeter using Rubidium Atoms

insights.claim: DARPA's GRAVMAP program was originally awarded to Vector Atomic in September 2025, with emphasis on reducing size, weight and power (SWaP) and manufacturability.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Manufacturability focus suggests a path toward production units rather than one-off prototypes.
insights.locator: Under DARPA's Gravimeter using Rubidium Atoms

insights.claim: Vector Atomic's Evergreen-30 iodine optical clock completed a 51-day U.S. Navy-sponsored deployment aboard the training ship TS Patriot State in 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Extended at-sea validation de-risks Navy procurement of commercial optical clocks.

insights.claim: The 51-day EG-30 deployment built on an earlier 21-day RIMPAC sea trial in which three units showed less than 300 ps/day drift.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Multi-unit, repeated naval trials indicate maturing field reliability.

insights.claim: The Evergreen-30 is a 3U 19-inch rackmount molecular iodine optical clock (29 L, 20 kg, 80 W) with 2.5e-14 instability at 1 s, under 4e-15/day drift, and 30-day holdover within 10 ns.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: 30-day holdover within 10 ns is the key spec for timing through prolonged GPS outages.

insights.claim: The EG-30 is a turnkey clock that needs no vacuum chamber or reference cavity and outputs 100 MHz, 10 MHz, 5 MHz and 1 PPS microwave signals alongside optical references, easing integration into existing systems.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Eliminating vacuum/cavity hardware is what makes optical clocks field-deployable and commercially scalable.
insights.quote: requires no vacuum chamber or reference cavity
insights.locator: Complementing its passive gravitational and magnetic navigation sensors

insights.claim: Vector Atomic's DUAL-OFC is a 9 L, 8 kg, under-25 W rackmount Er-fiber dual frequency comb at 1560 nm with better than 5e-17 stability at 1 s when optically referenced, supporting picosecond-level optical time transfer alongside the EG-30.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Comb plus clock gives IonQ a full optical timing/time-transfer product suite for defense networks.
insights.locator: PNT specifications table: Dual Optical Frequency Comb
